label: prop:alpha-em-categorical-trace-ratio
title: Algebraic identity: $\alpha_{EM} = h^2 / [q \cdot \delta_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta_q(T_{3,5})]$
html:
Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}] be the base ring. Let h = q - q^{-1} denote the skein parameter. Let T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} be the two genus-4-saturating torus knots (prop:force-carrier-bring-uniqueness). Let \delta_q denote the q-dimension decoration (def:delta-q-decoration). The bare electromagnetic fine-structure constant 1/\alpha_{EM} = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q (prop:em-coupling-projection) admits the categorical-trace-ratio decomposition:

  \boxed{\;\;
    \alpha_{EM}
    \;=\;
    \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot \delta_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta_q(T_{3,5})}
  \;\;}

Derivation

In the natural 2-strand representation, the categorical trace of a torus knot T_{2,k} sums the contributions from the irreducible Hecke representations V_{(2)} (eigenvalue q) and V_{(1,1)} (eigenvalue -q^{-1}). For odd k, this yields:

  \delta_q(T_{2,k})
  \;=\;
  q^{k} \cdot 1 + (-q^{-1})^{k} \cdot 1
  \;=\;
  q^{k} - q^{-k}.

Evaluating at k = 9 gives \delta_q(T_{2,9}) = q^{9} - q^{-9} = h\,[9]_q.

For the 3-strand torus knot T_{3,5}, the Rosso-Jones formula computes the categorical trace in H_3(q). Summing the contributions from V_{(3)}, V_{(2,1)}, and V_{(1,1,1)} with their respective eigenvalue powers yields \delta_q(T_{3,5}) = q^{10} - q^{-10} = h\,[10]_q.

Substitution produces the result:

  \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot \delta_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta_q(T_{3,5})}
  \;=\;
  \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot h\,[9]_q \cdot h\,[10]_q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q}
  \;=\;
  \alpha_{EM}.

\square

Numerical verification

Evaluation at q_0 \approx 1.1099786 yields an exact match to within 10^{-12}. See Table: Numerical verification of \alpha_{EM} trace-ratio.

⚠ This table is on a MUON pin; the block it derives from is on the PROTON pin (measured 2026-09-05, qou-i229; probe two_blocks_publish_the_two_sides_of_one_identity_at_different_pins_probe.py, 6/6). The identity above is exact at any q — \delta_q(T_{2,9}) = h[9]_q and \delta_q(T_{3,5}) = h[10]_q cancel the h^2, verified to 10^{-53} — so the two sides must agree numerically as well. They do not, because they are published at different anchors:

side block pin \alpha_{EM} \times 10^{3}
h^2/(q\,\delta_9\,\delta_{10}) this block muon 7.30870098
1/(q[9]_q[10]_q) prop:em-coupling-projection proton 7.30870156

A 7.94 \times 10^{-8} relative disagreement between two quantities this block proves equal. Determined by rounding every registered q_0 against all four table figures: the proton pin fails all four (residuals 1.0–1.5 \times 10^{-7}); every muon variant reproduces all four exactly.

Which muon vintage is not determined, and is not guessed here. The three registered muon values differ by 7.98 \times 10^{-11} relative; the sharpest figure in this table carries 9 significant digits and separating them needs about 12. Labelled rather than recomputed: the two blocks cannot both be right, and choosing between them is the anchor ruling qou-i229 holds, not a substitution.

Reproduce the table with two_blocks_publish_the_two_sides_of_one_identity_at_different_pins_probe.py.

Corrected 2026-09-05. This section previously read "The witness assertion validates this match: delta-q-decoration.witness.json." That witness declares a different block (def:delta-q-decoration), carries Markov-trace machinery rather than any of these four quantities, and is anchored q0Anchor: proton — so it validates nothing here and disagrees on the pin. This is why the candidate-producer sweep found no witness among 3277 carrying more than one of this table's figures.

Expressing the relationship as a trace ratio on the q-dimension layer reformulates existing projection identities.
